subject: Recap: Long-history summarization concerns + proposed evaluation
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Elizabeta Novak <elizabeta@chartwise.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Long-history summarization concerns + proposed evaluation

Hi Elizabeta — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned:

Call summary:
- Primary ask: reliably summarize multi-year patient visit histories without dropping salient events or introducing hallucinated diagnoses.
- Failure modes you flagged: truncation of earlier visits, decreased fidelity for timelines, and hallucinated procedure names when prompts include ambiguous shorthand.
- Current infra: Chartwise keeps raw notes in a centralized S3 bucket; typical documents are 3–20k tokens after OCR and de-identification.

Proposed evaluation approach (high-level):
1) Hand off a 200–500 record sample (anonymized) that captures long chronologies and edge-case shorthand.
2) Redwood runs a 2-week long-context eval: chunking + summarization flows, extractive verification, and a small human review panel for fidelity scoring.
3) We’ll return: per-record fidelity score, token cost estimates, latency percentiles, and a short-run canary config for pilot.

Model starts we recommend for the pilot (balanced perf/cost):
- Redwood-Instruct-13B (quantized) — strong instruction-following and cheaper for repeated summaries
- Llama-3-70B (float16) — better on very long coherence but higher cost; useful as an upper bound
- Open-Assistant-30B variant (q4) — good baseline for hallucination behavior

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Can you drop the sample (200 records) into the Drive folder we shared? I’ve attached a small formatting spec.
- Confirm whether you need a production SLA for the pilot or this is strictly evaluation.
- If you want, we’ll include a short prompt suite to stress-test timeline fidelity (will attach).

Attachments: chartwise_notes_sample.ndjson (3MB), call_recording_20270410.mp3 (8MB), summarization-prompt-suite.csv

Public links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFG_sample_eval (folder with spec + prompt set)

Thanks — I’ll put together a one-page evaluation plan and send internal ops notes to Ben/Neha.

— Avery

Thanks — quick answers inline and a more concrete plan below.

1) Cost estimate (rough):
- Redwood-Instruct-13B q4 pilot run + 10% human review: ~$5k–$9k for the 200-record sample (depends on average token counts — we’ll confirm after we inspect the sample).
- Llama-3-70B upper-bound run: ~3–4x the token cost.

2) Regression / quality tracking: yes — Redwood Optimize includes continuous quality monitoring tied to a prompt/eval suite. We version prompt sets and model pins. Typical guardrails we use:
- Baseline prompt/eval suite that runs on every rollout
- Token-level diff alerts (spike in generation tokens)
- Quality regression alerts (drop in fidelity score > 5 points) that can trigger automatic rollback to pinned model

3) Prompt suite: attached (summarization-prompt-suite.csv) and live in the Drive folder. It includes:
- 12 stress prompts targeting temporal fidelity (e.g., "List events in chronological order with dates and whether they relate to medication changes")
- 8 hallucination probes (ambiguous shorthand inputs)
- 5 extraction checks (verify key-value mapping: meds, dosages, procedures)

Concrete pilot plan (what we will deliver):
- Day 0–3: sample intake + quick data hygiene pass (formatting spec is attached)
- Day 4–10: run three model configs (13B q4, 30B q4, 70B fp16), generate summaries + extraction outputs
- Day 11–12: human review on a 10% stratified sample, fidelity scoring using our rubric
- Day 13–14: results pack (per-record fidelity, cost/latency tables, recommended canary config)

Ops notes (short):
- For your workflow, we recommend prefix caching for patient IDs and a 2k-token sliding window for timeline aggregation; that avoids reprocessing earlier tokens for each summary while keeping per-request latency shallow.
- If you expect >10 req/s at pilot scale, suggest a small dedicated pool (Redwood Dedicated) to stabilize p95 latency.

Attachments included: summarization-prompt-suite.csv, formatting-spec.md (in Drive).

Would you like us to schedule a short kickoff for Tue/Wed to accept credentials and confirm sample format?

— Avery

Subject: Internal: Chartwise pilot thresholds and ops items (do not forward)

Avery / Ben — internal ops note following the Chartwise thread. Please do NOT forward externally.

Quick checklist for the eval team:
- Acceptance criteria: mean fidelity >= 88% on the 200-sample set OR max hallucination rate < 6% (we’ll compute per-record).
- Canary config proposal: start with Redwood-Instruct-13B q4 pinned at 80% traffic, Llama-3-70B as 20% shadow for quality drift detection.
- Monitoring hooks: push per-token latencies and per-prompt fidelity to the Eval dashboard; set alert if fidelity delta > 5 pts in rolling 24h.
- Data handling: ensure all artifacts live in the Chartwise folder with restricted IAM read-only keys; rotate pre-signed URLs after intake.

Operational owners:
- Neha (lead on eval bench and human-review rubric)
- Ben (customer ops / ingress)
- Infra (I’ll tag later for dedicated pool sizing if pilot shows >10 req/s)

I’ve added the HubSpot reference and deal id CHRT-4821. Once sample drops, we’ll run the quick hygiene script and return a token/cost estimate.
